failure_modes.name: bearing_wear
failure_modes.description: Progressive degradation of rolling-element bearings due to lubricant breakdown, fatigue, or contamination. Increased metal-to-metal contact generates heat and broadband vibration as surface roughness develops on raceways and rolling elements.

symptoms.vibration_mm_s: Gradual rise from baseline 2.8 toward ISO zone C (>7.1 mm/s) over days to weeks; high-frequency components dominate
symptoms.temperature_c: Slow increase from baseline 62°C toward warning threshold 85°C as friction losses increase
symptoms.power_kw: Slight increase in late stages due to mechanical drag

failure_modes.typical_progression: Gradual onset over 2–8 weeks; accelerates sharply in final stage before failure
failure_modes.recommended_action: Replace bearing assembly; inspect lubricant supply and shaft alignment as root-cause contributors

failure_modes.name: cavitation
failure_modes.description: Formation and violent collapse of vapor bubbles inside the pump casing when inlet pressure drops below the fluid's vapor pressure. Bubble implosion causes micro-jet impacts on the impeller, leading to rapid material erosion and flow instability.

symptoms.vibration_mm_s: Erratic high-amplitude spikes superimposed on baseline; characteristic crackling noise in audible range
symptoms.pressure_bar: Sudden drop at inlet, typically below 2.0 bar; discharge pressure becomes unstable
symptoms.power_kw: Irregular fluctuation as flow breaks down

failure_modes.typical_progression: Sudden onset when operating conditions change (flow restriction, higher fluid temperature, speed increase); damage accumulates rapidly within hours
failure_modes.recommended_action: Inspect and clear inlet piping for blockages; verify NPSH margin; reduce pump speed or increase inlet pressure to restore stable operating point

failure_modes.name: misalignment
failure_modes.description: Angular or parallel offset between the pump shaft and driver (motor) shaft. Creates a cyclic load reversal once per revolution, placing abnormal stress on bearings, seals, and the coupling. Often introduced during installation or after maintenance.

symptoms.vibration_mm_s: Persistently elevated from startup; dominant 1× and 2× running-speed frequency components; typically 4.5–8.0 mm/s
symptoms.temperature_c: Mildly elevated at bearing housings due to increased radial load
symptoms.power_kw: Consistently 10–20% above normal baseline due to extra mechanical losses in coupling and bearings

failure_modes.typical_progression: Constant from installation or restart after maintenance; does not worsen in early stages but accelerates bearing and seal wear over months
failure_modes.recommended_action: Laser-align shaft coupling to within ±0.05 mm parallel and ±0.05 mm/100 mm angular tolerance; re-check after thermal stabilisation

failure_modes.name: seal_leakage
failure_modes.description: Failure of the mechanical seal between the rotating shaft and the pump casing, allowing process fluid to escape. Causes include wear of seal faces, spring fatigue, chemical attack, or running dry. Results in pressure loss, environmental contamination, and accelerated shaft wear.

symptoms.vibration_mm_s: Slightly elevated if leakage causes imbalanced hydraulic forces
symptoms.temperature_c: Unaffected unless dry-running heats seal faces
symptoms.pressure_bar: Gradual decline in discharge pressure as internal leakage increases; may drop 0.5–1.5 bar below expected
symptoms.power_kw: Mild reduction as effective flow decreases; pump runs off best-efficiency point

failure_modes.typical_progression: Gradual over days to weeks; early signs are minor weeping around the seal housing before full leakage develops
failure_modes.recommended_action: Replace mechanical seal faces and secondary seals; inspect shaft sleeve for scoring; verify correct flush plan (API Plan 11 or 32)

failure_modes.name: imbalance
failure_modes.description: Uneven mass distribution on the rotating impeller, caused by erosion, fouling build-up, or blade damage. Generates a centrifugal force rotating at shaft speed that excites radial vibration, shortening bearing and seal life.

symptoms.vibration_mm_s: Elevated broadband vibration with a sharp dominant peak at 1× running speed; typically 5.0–9.0 mm/s
symptoms.temperature_c: Mildly elevated at bearing housings from increased radial load
symptoms.pressure_bar: Slightly reduced if blade damage has decreased hydraulic efficiency
symptoms.power_kw: Marginally increased due to additional radial bearing forces

failure_modes.typical_progression: Gradual increase as erosion or fouling accumulates; can be sudden if a blade chip or foreign object impact occurs
failure_modes.recommended_action: Remove impeller; clean or replace if eroded; dynamic balance to ISO 1940 Grade G2.5 before reinstallation
